title: Parmigiana di Zucchine
subtitle: Layered courgette, tomato, and mozzarella bake
excerpt: Parmigiana di zucchine is the courgette version of the famous aubergine dish: courgette slices fried or grilled until golden, then layered with tomato sauce, mozzarella, and Parmigiano in a baking dish and baked until bubbling. It is lighter than the aubergine version and excellent in late summer when courgettes are at their best.
sourceNotes: Parmigiana di zucchine is a Campanian and southern Italian variation of parmigiana di melanzane, using courgette in place of aubergine. Both dishes are documented throughout the Italian south; the courgette version is particularly popular in Campania and Calabria.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble a day ahead and refrigerate unbaked. Bake directly from the fridge, adding 10 minutes to the cooking time. The baked dish also keeps for 2 days and reheats well.

content.text: Parmigiana di zucchine layers fried or grilled courgette with tomato sauce and mozzarella, then bakes it into a cohesive, deeply savoury whole. The courgettes must be well coloured before layering: pale, steamed courgettes produce a watery, flavourless result. Pat them dry after frying and let the dish rest after baking so the layers can settle.

items.prepNote: 2 x 400 g tins, or 700 g fresh
fior di latte, thinly sliced and dried on paper

content.text: Pat the courgette slices dry with paper towel. Heat sunflower oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the courgette in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden. Don't crowd the pan: they will steam rather than fry. Drain on paper towel and season lightly.
Warm the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the garlic for 1 to 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes, crush, and simmer for 15 minutes until thickened. Season and stir in the basil.

Heat the oven to 190°C fan. Spoon a thin layer of tomato sauce over the base of a deep baking dish. Layer courgette slices over, then mozzarella, then a spoonful of tomato sauce, then Parmigiano. Repeat until all ingredients are used, finishing with tomato sauce and Parmigiano.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest for 15 minutes before serving: the layers settle as it cools slightly, making it easier to cut and serve.

items.cause: Courgettes were not fried enough or mozzarella was too wet
items.fix: Fry the courgettes until properly golden: the colour is the indication of reduced moisture. Dry mozzarella on paper for at least 30 minutes.

items.symptom: Top is browned but centre is cold
items.cause: Dish went into the oven too cold or oven was too hot
items.fix: Bring to room temperature before baking. If the top is browning too fast, cover with foil and continue baking until heated through.

content.text: Parmigiana di zucchine uses the same idea as the aubergine version. A vegetable is fried until golden, layered with tomato and cheese, and baked. It is a late-summer dish, made when courgettes and tomatoes are both in season. In Campania it is often eaten at lunch, made ahead and served at room temperature.
